correctness.rationale: With P=1u, A^k=P+t(I−P), t=(−1/(n−1))^k, and BP=P, so C_k=(1−t)P+tB. For k odd the worst possible entry is bounded below by (1−t)/n+t; this is positive for k≥3, and at k=1 strictness follows from B_ij<1 (at least two neighbors). Even k is a strictly positive mixture. Stationarity gives ν=(1−t)u(I−tB)⁻¹. Reversibility transfers this resolvent to the density h=u/π in L²(π). Each nonconstant mode of h is scaled by f_λ(t)=(1−t)/(1−tλ)>0, strictly decreasing because λ<1. Thus χ² is a sum of squared coefficients times f_λ², and the inverse-degree opinion is ηh, giving a sum of the same squares times f_λ after subtracting c_B=η. The imbalance vanishes exactly for equal weighted degrees, so both chains have the stated strictness, parity, and limits. On the quotient by constants the kernel acts as tB, giving exactly the non-Perron eigenvalues. Looplessness gives their B-eigenvalue sum −1, so ρ₂(B)≥1/(n−1). Equality would make all those eigenvalues −1/(n−1); reversibility and the zero diagonal then force π=u and B=A. Hence (n−1)ρ₂(B)>1 in the irregular case and its power 1/(k+1) strictly decreases, giving the per-step result.
residual_risks: Read ‘odd switching period’ in the prose as odd complete-layer length k, i.e. an even total cycle length k+1; the displayed claims use k consistently.
The opinion chain is for the inverse-degree witness, not all opinions. Recorded finite rational tests corroborate examples and the quotient action, not the all-graph spectral and parity statements.

value.rationale: The precise parity obstruction for every irregular supported network turns a one-off noninterpolation phenomenon into a sharp structural law with an exact regularity boundary. The bounded inverse-degree witness turns a distributional comparison into an observable consensus, while the exact contraction factor distinguishes influence bias from the speed of convergence.
residual_risks: Specific deterministic switch order and complete loopless layer; no assertion for directed, generic asynchronous, or arbitrary opinion inputs.
